meta.name: Castrol India Ltd
meta.about: Castrol India Ltd is principally engaged in the business of manufacturing & marketing of automotive and industrial lubricants and related services.[1]
meta.keyPoints: Parentage[1][2] The company is part of the BP group, a global integrated energy company engaged across oil and gas, fuels and convenience, EV charging, supply and trading, shipping, and energy technology. In Dec 2025, British Petroleum announced an agreement to sell a 65% stake in the company to Stonepeak at an enterprise value of approximately US$10 Bn, while retaining a 35% minority stake. The transaction is now completed and Stonepeak, a Private Equity player has recenty acquired the Castrol business from its parent British Petroleum and hence, there is now a change in the parentage of the company.
pros: Stock is providing a good dividend yield of 4.61%.
Company has a good return on equity (ROE) track record: 3 Years ROE 43.4%
Company has been maintaining a healthy dividend payout of 109%
cons: Stock is trading at 9.84 times its book value

growth.text: Revenue compounded at 5.7% a year over 10 years (5y: 13.8%, 3y: 6.2%), from ₹3,298 cr to ₹5,722 cr.
Profit grew 4.4% a year over the same decade — slower than revenue, i.e. margins leaked.
Worst profit year: Dec20 (-29.5%); best: Dec21 (+30.0%).

margins.text: EBITDA margin has ranged 21.2%–29.8% since Dec14 (peak Dec19, trough Dec14); Dec25 was 23.6%.
Q2FY27 operating margin of 15.1% is lower than 90.8% of the 87 quarters on record — near the bottom of its history.

returns.text: ROE was 45.5% in Dec25 (range 41.9–114.7% since Dec14).
Stripping out cash and investments, return on operating capital was 327.9% vs headline ROCE of 60.0% — the idle cash is diluting reported returns.
DuPont Dec25: net margin 16.6% × asset turnover 1.6x × leverage 1.7x.

balance.text: Net cash of ₹1,521 cr (cash + investments less borrowings), 80.0% of net worth.

cash.text: Over 12 years the business generated ₹9,414 cr of operating cash flow (106.0% of reported profit), spent ₹863 cr on capex and paid ₹7,146 cr in dividends.
Dec25 capex was 1.0x depreciation and 1.7% of sales — maintenance-level spending.
Cash conversion cycle of 0 days in Dec25.

valuation.text: P/E of 18.3x vs 10-year median 19.4x (range 11.8–33.4x); cheaper than 62.0% of that period.
EV/EBITDA of 11.9x vs 10-year median 12.1x (range 7.2–19.9x); cheaper than 54.7% of that period.
P/B of 9.9x vs 10-year median 9.7x (range 5.7–31.5x); cheaper than 44.4% of that period.
At its 10-year median P/E on current earnings, the stock would be ~₹202 vs ₹190 today (6.1%).

price.text: Stock up 0.7% over 1 year; 5y CAGR 7.2%, 10y CAGR -0.3%. Currently 28.6% below its all-time high of ₹267.
Versus BSE-500: 0.7% vs -10.7% over 1 year; since 2019, 3.2% vs 11.3% a year.

ownership.text: Domestic institutions cut their stake from 15.9% to 12.9% over 12 quarters.
